subject: Request: temporary SLO carveout + conditional pricing concession (PulseMetrics pilot)
messages:
From: Sam Torres <s.torres@pulsemetrics.io>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Aisha Raman <aisha@pulsemetrics.io>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Pilot SLA ask + pricing follow-up

Irene — thanks again for the demo last week. We’re excited to move the PulseMetrics pilot into production next month; two asks from our side before we sign the MPA: 1) a temporary SLO carveout for the first 90 days (allow uptime floor of 97% for the pilot) and 2) a capped service-credit exposure during that window (we’d like a fixed credit cap to align with our internal finance rules).

We understand this is nonstandard. In exchange we can commit to a 12-month early-bird pricing and a volume commitment if the pilot passes our ops checks. Can your team outline how Redwood would structure the remedy and what commercial tradeoffs look like?

Attachments: PulseMetrics_MutualActionPlan_v2.pdf

—Sam
Sam Torres
Head of Platform Engineering | PulseMetrics
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Sam Torres <s.torres@pulsemetrics.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 21 Mar 2027 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA ask + pricing follow-up

Sam — appreciate the clarity and the trade. High level thoughts: we can consider a temporary SLO floor qualified as a pilot concession, but we need exec sign-off for any change that reduces uptime obligations and for a fixed credit cap. Marissa — can you put together the commercial impact (forecasted unit economics delta) and the precise remedy table (credits per outage bucket) so I can escalate? Ben — heads up, this will touch quota/discount stack.

I’ll coordinate timing for a 15-min alignment with Deal Desk so we can get to a clear ask for the exec review.

Thanks,
Irene
Irene Choi
Director, Enterprise Sales | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA ask + pricing follow-up

Team — attached is a proposed remedy table and the commercial delta for a 90-day pilot carveout. Key points:
- Proposed concession: temporary uptime target lowered to 97% for first 90 days only.
- Service credit: one-time fixed cap equal to 1.5x average monthly invoice during pilot (protects both sides).
- Pricing: 15% early-bird discount for 12 months, conditional on pilot completion and telemetry sharing.
- Conditions: pilot limited to single region, dedicated preemptible burst disabled, Redwood observability hooks enabled (request pulse metrics feed).

If execs sign this, legal needs to add a pilot addendum with explicit timebox and telemetry obligations. Karthik — can you confirm the redline language we need?

Attachments: proposed-remedy-table.xlsx

—Marissa
Head of Deal Desk | Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 23 Mar 2027 09:11:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Pilot SLA ask + pricing follow-up

I reviewed Marissa’s draft. Legal is comfortable with a 90-day carveout provided the addendum includes:
- explicit timebox (start/end dates),
- telemetry & runbook access obligations,
- rollback clause if production issues persist beyond pilot, and
- a single acceptance gate that triggers standard SLA reinstatement.

I recommend we limit precedent by making this pilot-specific, non-precedential language and requiring CISO review for any telemetry contract.

—Karthik
Senior Counsel, Commercial Contracts | Redwood Inference
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: Exec summary and conditional approval request for CFO/CEO review

Irene/Marissa — I’ve summarized the ask for executive consideration. Recommendation: approve the 90-day SLO carveout with the fixed credit cap (1.5x monthly) on the following conditions:
1) It’s explicitly timeboxed (90 days) and limited to the PulseMetrics pilot and region us-west-2.
2) PulseMetrics must enable Redwood telemetry feeds and monthly operations reviews.
3) Pricing trade: 15% early-bird for 12 months and a minimum committed spend of $200k over 12 months.
4) Legal to include non-precedential clause and require CISO signoff on telemetry terms.

If both CFO and CEO sign off (I’ll route to them today), we can issue a pilot addendum and get DocuSign started. Please confirm final language and I’ll escalate.

—Ben
VP, Commercial | Redwood Inference
